reviews.review_title: Pure VR Madness at Its Best!
reviews.review_description:
Car Crash Arena isn’t just fun—it’s pure, unfiltered madness! This indie gem delivers non-stop adrenaline in the best way possible, reminding me of the legendary FlatOut 4: Total Insanity VR. But here’s the kicker: it’s a standalone game, and the fluidity? Incredible. What an amazing surprise!
Every aspect of this game screams arcade perfection. You’ve got varied opponents to crush, upgrades to unlock, and a wave system that keeps the chaos fresh. Whether you’re driving from inside your car or hanging onto the hood, the controls are top-notch. The turning is smooth, intuitive, and—most importantly—won’t make you sick, which is a huge win for VR racing games.
And let’s talk about the devs—they’re relentless. Bugs get squashed fast, new arenas to come, and the game just keeps getting better. If you love high-octane, chaotic fun, this is a must-play. Trust me, you’ll be hooked from the first crash! 🎮🔥

Car Crash Arena delivers exactly what it promises: fast, chaotic and satisfying vehicle combat. Smashing opponents with well-timed boosts while avoiding arena hazards creates a fun gameplay loop that's easy to jump into.

For a solo indie project, it's an impressive foundation with plenty of potential. The core mechanics are enjoyable, and I can easily see this becoming even better with future updates. Looking forward to seeing how the game evolves!

I think this is a valiant effort and appreciate the work gone into this game. I could see the vision in the gameplay trailer and thought I have to get behind this. 

No it's not perfect and I didn't expect that.

Bur what is showcased here is only about 10% away from being a good quality title. 

The only thing missing is car damage, even if it's just the textures that change from clean paint to cracks and scratches (I understand the quest has limitations so a texture swap for now will be a quick fix). Just so it adds a bit of visual immersion.

Also some basic particles when crashing would help also. 

1 handed steering should be made better as the handling using controllers to steer is a bit rough, with no settings to dial it in. 

A resolution bump wouldn't go a miss as the resolution is just about OK and serviceable as it is but needs improvement.

And obviously more levels, pickups, weapons would be great too. 

And multiplayer of course. 

But I reckon people would get behind this game. It's what VR is crying out for. A twisted metal type game. 

Loving the cars, the overall vibe though. Dont give up. I got ya back.
